intro.text: Founded in 1964 and headquartered in Cincinnati, Hillman is a leading provider of hardware and related products serving retail, pro distribution, and industrial customers. Over the last 60-plus years, Hillman has built a legacy of service and growth by forming strategic partnerships with North America’s leading home improvement, hardware, and farm and fleet retailers. Hillman differentiates itself from the competition with its dedicated field sales team of 1,200+ associates, direct-to-store distribution capabilities, and world class global sourcing and supply chain expertise.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: We sell our products to a large volume of customers, the top two of which accounted for approximately $674.3 million, or approximately 43% of our total revenues in 2025.

For the year ended December 27, 2025, Home Depot was the single largest customer, representing approximately $349.9 million or 22.5% of our total revenues and Lowe's was the second largest customer at approximately $324.4 million or 20.9% of our total revenues.
No other customer accounted for more than 10% of total revenues in 2025.
For the year ended December 27, 2025, the largest two customers, Lowe's and Home Depot, accounted for 43.4 % of total revenues and 28.7 % of the year-end accounts receivable balance.
For the year ended December 28, 2024, the largest two customers accounted for 40.9 % of total revenues and 32.6 % of the year end accounts receivable balance.
Except as described in the paragraphs above, no other customer accounted for more than 10% of the Company's accounts receivables in 2025 or 2024.
You should not rely on these forward-looking statements as predictions of future events.

We currently manage a worldwide supply chain comprised of a large number of vendors, the largest of which accounted for approximately 7.6% of the Company's annual purchases and the top five of which accounted for approximately 17.2% of our annual purchases.
In addition, we are the primary supplier of Metal Shapes to many wholesalers throughout the country.

The Company does not believe a sales concentration exists in these scenarios, as the independently owned hardware stores can continue to make purchases from the Company via a direct bill arrangement or via another purchasing cooperative.
The success of our efforts to grow our business depends on the contributions and abilities of key executives, our sales force, and other personnel.

Our long-term success in the current competitive environment depends on our ability to develop and commercialize a continuing stream of innovative new products which create and maintain consumer demand.
We import a majority of our products and rely on foreign sources, primarily China and Taiwan, to meet our supply demands at prices that support our current operating margins.

However, it is not always possible to replace a vendor on short notice without disruption in our operations, which may require more costly expedited transportation expense and replacement of a major vendor is often at higher prices.
Because our business is working capital intensive, we rely on our ability to manage our product purchasing and customer credit policies.
Successful sales and marketing efforts depend on our ability to recruit and retain qualified employees.

The success of our efforts to grow our business depends on the contributions and abilities of key executives, our sales force, and other personnel, including the ability of our sales force to achieve adequate customer coverage.

We depend on our information systems, and those of our third party vendors and business partners, to process orders, to manage inventory and accounts receivable collections, to purchase, sell, and ship products efficiently and on a timely basis, to maintain cost-effective operations, and to provide superior service to our customers.
We rely on various information systems and technology to manage our business.

We rely on available borrowings under the Asset-Based Revolving credit facility (“ABL Revolver”) for cash to operate our business, and the availability of credit under the ABL Revolver may be subject to significant fluctuation.
A 5% difference in actual excess and obsolete inventory reserved for at December 27, 2025 would have affected net earnings by approximately $1.6 million in fiscal 2025.
